title: Provider-neutral Forge seam for osf
summary: Introduces a provider-neutral `Forge` trait as the seam between the osf CLI and a code host, with three implementations: an in-memory `FakeForge` test double, a `report_change` engine step that runs open-PR → status block → capabilities → review → checks in one fixed order, and a `GitHub` adapter that drives the `gh` command line. The CLI's `review post`, `pr status apply` and `pr status refresh` paths now go through the trait, and the process-spawning code that used to live in `review.rs` and `pr_status.rs` has moved into the adapter, leaving those modules pure.

lanes.subtitle: commands and callers
lanes.summary: The command-line entry points that build a forge and drive it: review post, pr status apply, pr status refresh, and the review-run post path.

lanes.label: Forge seam
lanes.subtitle: provider-neutral trait and engine step
lanes.summary: The new provider-neutral layer: the Forge trait, its data types, and the report_change engine step that fixes the order of operations.

nodes.label: osf CLI
nodes.subtitle: main.rs command dispatch
nodes.summary: The binary's command handlers. review post, pr status apply and pr status refresh now build a GitHub adapter and call it through the Forge trait instead of shelling out directly.

nodes.label: review post
nodes.subtitle: review_post_cmd
nodes.summary: Reads the head commit through the adapter, builds a review plan, and posts it through the forge. Dry-run still prints the payload without touching the network.

nodes.label: pr status apply
nodes.subtitle: pr_status_apply_cmd
nodes.summary: Dry-run reads the body through the adapter's client; the real path calls write_status_block on the forge, which reads, applies the block and edits.

nodes.label: pr status refresh
nodes.subtitle: pr_status_refresh_cmd
nodes.summary: Gathers tier, gates and review data, then writes the status block through the forge. Gates now come from a forge check-status read rather than a direct gh call.

nodes.label: review run --post-to
nodes.subtitle: post_run_outcome
nodes.summary: The review-run post path now reads the head commit through the adapter and posts through the forge, reporting advisory fallbacks from PostedReview.

nodes.label: github_adapter()
nodes.subtitle: the only place that builds GitHub<RealGh>
nodes.summary: A single constructor for the real adapter, so the CLI has exactly one place that names the provider.

nodes.label: Forge trait
nodes.subtitle: create_branch, open_pull_request, write_status_block, post_review, read_check_status, capabilities
nodes.summary: The provider-neutral seam. Six operations, all taking plain data types, none naming a provider, URL or command. Object-safe and Send + Sync.

nodes.label: Forge data types
nodes.subtitle: PullRequestId, NewBranch, NewReview, PostedReview, Capabilities, ReadOutcome
nodes.summary: The plain serializable structs and enums that cross the seam. ReadOutcome distinguishes found, empty and unknown; VerdictCapability and ReadCapability describe what an identity may do.

nodes.label: report_change
nodes.subtitle: the Report step as provider-neutral run code
nodes.summary: Runs one fixed order: open the pull request, write the status block, read capabilities, post the review only when the identity may, then read the check status. A failed step stops the run and names itself.

nodes.label: ReportError / Step
nodes.subtitle: which step failed and why
nodes.summary: Names the failed step (open pull request, write status block, check capabilities, post review) alongside the forge error, so a caller can tell where a run stopped.

nodes.label: FakeForge
nodes.subtitle: in-memory Forge, records every call
nodes.summary: A test double that performs no process, file, network or clock work. It records each call as plain data and can script a sequence of answers per operation, repeating the last once the script runs out.

nodes.label: Script<T>
nodes.subtitle: ordered answers with a cursor
nodes.summary: Holds a vector of answers and a mutex-guarded cursor; take_next repeats the final answer once the script is exhausted.

nodes.label: GitHub<C>
nodes.subtitle: the first Forge adapter
nodes.summary: Wraps a GhClient and implements Forge by building argv and JSON payloads, running them, and parsing the responses. Also exposes head_commit for the review anchor.

nodes.label: RealGh
nodes.subtitle: spawns the gh command
nodes.summary: The only code that starts a process. It runs gh with piped stdio, writes stdin when given, and reads the body, review, PR info, checks and edit operations.

nodes.label: GhClient trait
nodes.subtitle: run, view_body, view_review, view_pr_info, view_checks, edit_body
nodes.summary: The existing client trait gained a raw run method taking argv and optional stdin, so the adapter can drive arbitrary gh commands while tests still supply a fake.

nodes.label: pr_status (pure)
nodes.subtitle: parse_checks, gates_from_checks, apply
nodes.summary: Lost its process-spawning RealGh and gained parse_checks plus gates_from_checks, so the checks JSON is read into triples and the gate spec is built from them separately.

nodes.label: review (pure)
nodes.subtitle: plan, payload, classify, after_first_attempt
nodes.summary: Lost fetch_head_sha and post_via_gh; parse_head_sha_json is now public so the adapter can use it. The module holds no process or network call.

nodes.label: gh CLI
nodes.subtitle: installed command line tool
nodes.summary: The installed gh binary the adapter spawns. Unchanged by this diff; it is the boundary the seam exists to isolate.

nodes.label: GitHub API
nodes.subtitle: refs, pulls, reviews, checks
nodes.summary: The remote API gh talks to: branch refs, pull requests, reviews and check runs. Reached only through the adapter.

nodes.label: forge_callers tests
nodes.subtitle: characterization tests over a fake gh script
nodes.summary: Drives review post, pr status apply and pr status refresh against a fake gh shell script first on PATH, pinning the exact call list, payloads and failure text of the three commands.

nodes.label: forge_fake_run test
nodes.subtitle: a full run on the in-memory double
nodes.summary: Runs create_branch then report_change entirely against FakeForge, asserting the full call list and that a failed status block stops the run before the review.

views.title: Forge seam in context
views.summary: The osf CLI reaches the code host through the new provider-neutral Forge trait. Two adapters implement it: the in-memory FakeForge for tests and the GitHub adapter that spawns gh.
